Title: Analyst, Analytics, Data Science
Description: Rise is an award-winning , full-service Media Agency of Record that is backed by data and powered by people. We create omnichannel experiences using our proprietary tech stack and advanced analytics capabilities to help solve the unique struggles brands face today. This approach, with transparency at its core , specializes in omnichannel media, commerce and retail media, advanced in-home media, as well as content and creator marketing. We offer "Risers" the opportunity to work in an ever-evolving industry that will foster learning and development, provide an innovative work environment with diverse projects and clients, career advancement paths a collaborative team environment, corporate social responsibility initiatives, an inclusive and diverse culture, plus association with a reputable media agency. We're looking for talent like you who can continue to elevate our work and culture. GENERAL PURPOSE OF JOB As a Data Scientist on Quad's Insights and Analytics team, you will play an important role in driving the effectiveness of media campaigns through advanced data analysis. You will be responsible for executing modeling projects using a variety of home-grown and 3rd-party tools. This includes data cleansing, formatting, loading, execution, model evaluation, and result reviews. In collaboration with the broader team, you will help craft the insights from these models and turn those insights into recommendations for our clients. Throughout the process, we expect you to seek ways to improve the processes. Location: Mexico City, 3 days in office; Applicants must hold Mexican citizenship Key Responsibilities Model Execution: Load, execute, and refine statistical and machine learning models to assess and improve media effectiveness. Develop processes and data pipelines to support media planning and optimization. Data Analysis: Conduct thorough analyses of media performance data, including engagement metrics, conversion rates, and ROI. Identify trends, patterns, and insights to inform media strategy. Insights Generation: Translate complex data findings into clear, actionable insights. Prepare detailed reports and visualizations that communicate the impact and effectiveness of media strategies. Collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams, including media planners, marketing strategists, and data engineers, to ensure alignment of data insights with overall media strategy. Continuous Improvement: Stay curious about the latest industry trends and advancements in data science and media analytics. Propose and implement improvements to existing models and methodologies. Job Requirements Proven experience in data science, particularly in building and deploying predictive, explanatory, or decomposition models. Strong proficiency in statistical analysis and machine learning techniques. Experience with data visualization tools and techniques for effective communication of insights. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present complex data clearly and understandably. Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team. Good English proficiency, recognizing that your manager is bilingual and will aid where necessary. Education Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related field. A Master's degree or higher is preferred. Experience Minimum of 1-3 years of experience in data science or analytics, with a focus on media effectiveness, marketing analytics, or related areas. Experience working in an agency or client-facing role is a plus. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Technical Skills: Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R. Experience with data manipulation and analysis libraries (e.g., Pandas, NumPy) and machine learning frameworks (e.g., Scikit-learn, TensorFlow), mathematical and statistical modeling, Bayesian methods, optimization techniques, and simulation. Data Tools: Expertise in SQL for querying databases, and familiarity with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar. Analytical Thinking: Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to interpret data and develop actionable insights. Communication: Ability to convey complex data insights and technical information to non-technical stakeholders. Time Management: Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines. Collaboration: Strong team player with experience working in a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Marketing Interest and Initiative: Strong interest in marketing and a proactive attitude toward learning new concepts, tools, and strategies, with the initiative to apply knowledge and contribute to business objectives.

Title: Coordinación Data Science - PSC
Description: Ubicación: Oficina Central Inglés: Avanzado Resumen de posición Desarrollar e implementar soluciones digitales enfocadas en la automatización, visualización, modelado y análisis de datos, que permitan acelerar la toma de decisiones ágiles y generar valor para el negocio, con especial foco en la mejora del forecast de Demand Planning. Las principales tareas del rol son: Desarrollo de herramientas de visualización: Diseñar e implementar dashboards y herramientas de visualización que permitan identificar oportunidades, riesgos y desviaciones en los procesos de DSP y Supply Planning. Automatización de procesos: Desarrollar RPAs, aplicaciones y scripts utilizando SAS, Python, R y SQL, con el objetivo de reducir los tiempos destinados a la construcción y procesamiento de información. Soporte a la toma de decisiones: Aplicar métodos matemáticos, estadísticos y de machine learning para transformar datos en información relevante que facilite decisiones ágiles y contribuya a resolver retos del negocio. Modelado y análisis de datos: Desarrollar modelos descriptivos, predictivos y prescriptivos que permitan identificar tendencias, anticipar escenarios y mejorar la precisión del pronóstico de demanda. Generación y comunicación de insights de negocio: Analizar información, realizar diagnósticos e identificar patrones, causas raíz, riesgos y oportunidades, transformando los resultados técnicos en recomendaciones claras y accionables. Comunicar los hallazgos mediante storytelling y presentaciones ejecutivas que faciliten la toma de decisiones con equipos de DSP, Supply Planning, mercados y áreas corporativas. ¿Qué te hará exitoso? Formación universitaria en Actuaría, Matemáticas, Matemáticas Aplicadas, Ciencia de Datos, Estadística, Economía, Negocios o áreas afines. Experiencia mínima de 2 años como científico/a de datos, analista de datos, analista de Business Intelligence, especialista de Machine Learning, consultor/a de análisis de datos o posiciones similares. Experiencia en Data Science, Data Analytics, estadística, análisis de datos e identificación de insights de negocio. Conocimientos de programación y análisis de datos con SAS, R y Python. Manejo intermedio de SAS, Power BI y Python. Inglés avanzado, indispensable para la interacción con mercados y equipos corporativos. Habilidades sólidas de comunicación, presentación de resultados y storytelling para traducir análisis técnicos en información comprensible para el negocio.

Title: Business Intelligence Engineer, Supply Chain Business Insights
Description: Description Help shape the data foundation behind one of Amazon's fastest-growing supply chain networks — and put AI in the hands of the people who move millions of packages across Mexico every day. This is your chance to build the pipelines, analytics, and cloud-native solutions that turn raw data into trusted, accurate intelligence for an organization at the forefront of GenAI adoption. As a Business Intelligence Engineer on the MX Supply Chain BI team, you will design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines, reporting solutions, and analytical tools that power decisions across Mexico's Supply Chain — from network planning and capacity to last mile operations. You will work with large-scale datasets on AWS, write production-grade Python code, deploy cloud-based solutions, and partner with stakeholders across 10 functional areas to deliver insights that drive operational performance. You will contribute to the team's AI-ready data lakehouse platform and help embed GenAI and ML capabilities into the analytics portfolio. Key job responsibilities Design, develop, and maintain scalable ETL/big-data pipelines using AWS services following medallion-architecture best practices Write production-grade Python code for data transformation, automation, statistical analysis, and integration with AI/ML workflows Build high quality datasets with robust metadata for agents to consume and give insights to our stakeholders. Deploy and manage cloud-native data solutions on AWS through infrastructure-as-code based deployments. Collaborate with stakeholders across Supply Chain functional areas (Topology, S&OP, Network Planning, Middle Mile, Last Mile, Sort Centers, Operations) to translate business questions into analytical solutions Contribute to the team's AI-ready data lakehouse platform (Apache Iceberg on serverless AWS), ensuring data quality, governance, and single-source-of-truth standards Write and optimize complex queries on SQL, Spark SQL and PySpark across large-scale datasets to support reporting, ad-hoc analysis, and metric development Establish and follow engineering best practices including code reviews, testing, monitoring, documentation, and logging best practices. Proactively identify opportunities to improve data availability, reduce time-to-insight, and automate manual reporting processes Support the team's GenAI/ML initiatives by preparing governed, high-quality datasets and contributing to data products that enable agentic and self-service AI workflows A day in the life You start your morning reviewing pipeline health dashboards and resolving any data quality alerts from overnight ETL runs. By mid-morning, you're deep in Python — building a new data transformation module. After a quick stand-up with your peers, you jump into a working session with a Last Mile stakeholder who needs a new metric added to their operational dashboard; you scope the requirement, write the code and push for your peers to review before lunch. You wrap up the day by prototyping a data integration that will expose a new dataset to the team's GenAI agent through the MCP — a small step that will let operations leaders ask natural-language questions about network speed and compliance. No two days are the same, but every day your work makes Supply Chain decisions faster, smarter, and more trusted. About The Team MX Supply Chain Business Insights owns the data, insights, and analytics that power how Amazon's Mexico Supply Chain organization understands its business, measures its customer experience, and makes decisions. The team serves 10 functional areas with growing cross-LATAM collaboration with Brazil. Our team works together to deliver the data infrastructure, pipelines, semantic layers, and reporting that underpin MX Supply Chain's most critical business metrics, while also developing full stack applications to gather and process data. We are at an inflection point: as we embed GenAI across the portfolio and scale an AI-ready data lakehouse across LATAM, the decisions our stakeholders make depend on data they can trust, access quickly, and act on confidently. Basic Qualifications 3+ years of analyzing and interpreting data with Redshift, Oracle, NoSQL etc. experience Experience using Python scripting to process data for modeling 3+ years of processing large, multi-dimensional datasets from multiple sources experience Experience using SQL (Structured Query Language) to pull data from a database or data warehouse Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines Bachelor's degree or above in business administration, finance, economics, computer science, data science, engineering, or other related field, or 2+ years of Amazon RME (BB/3P) Full Time Exempt experience Experience using SQL to pull data from a database or data warehouse and scripting experience (Python) to process data for modeling Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools Experience with AI/ML technologies Experience building and operating a cloud-based architecture Preferred Qualifications Experience with AWS solutions such as EC2, DynamoDB, S3, and Redshift Experience in data mining, ETL, etc. and using databases in a business environment with large-scale, complex datasets Experience developing and presenting recommendations of new metrics allowing better understanding of the performance of the business Experience with forecasting and statistical analysis Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Title: Analista de Datos y Estructuración de Energía
Description: Descripción ¿Te apasiona el sector energético y disfrutas descifrando grandes volúmenes de datos para impulsar decisiones comerciales reales? Si tienes formación técnica, dominas herramientas de análisis y buscas un espacio donde tu curiosidad analítica acelere tu carrera en energías renovables, ¡queremos conocerte! ¿Quiénes somos? Desde Adecco trabajamos con Grupo Enel donde impulsamos la transición hacia un futuro energético sostenible. Somos un equipo dinámico enfocado en el suministro calificado y proyectos renovables, donde valoramos la innovación, la autonomía y el talento joven con ganas de trascender. Resumen del rol Buscamos un/a Analista de Datos y Estructuración de Energía para unirse al equipo de Front Office. Tu misión principal será procesar y analizar información compleja del Mercado Eléctrico Mexicano (incluyendo precios spot y datos comerciales) para estructurar ofertas de suministro atractivas, operando como el pilar analítico detrás de la estrategia comercial (sin exposición directa a clientes). Responsabilidades clave Procesar, limpiar y analizar grandes volúmenes de bases de datos horarias y precios spot . Dar soporte analítico en los procesos de adquisición de energía y generación de ofertas comerciales. Optimizar modelos y scripts de análisis de datos para agilizar la evaluación de escenarios de mercado. Colaborar estrechamente con el equipo comercial aportando inteligencia analítica basada en datos sólidos. Anticipar y resolver retos operativos del día a día con una actitud proactiva y resolutiva. Requisitos técnicos Formación en ingeniería (Eléctrica, Mecánica, Industrial) o carreras afines con sólidos fundamentos cuantitativos/físicos. Manejo avanzado de bases de datos y herramientas ofimáticas (Excel avanzado, SQL). Familiaridad con el Mercado Eléctrico Mexicano o gran entusiasmo por aprenderlo rápidamente. Experiencia o proyectos académicos/laborales utilizando Python para análisis de datos y automatización. Uso de herramientas de visualización como Power BI. 1 a 2 años de experiencia o recién egresados con alto potencial. Lo que te encantará Trabajarás con un equipo experto que disfruta enseñando y colaborando. Aquí no vienes a replicar tareas mecánicas, sino a aportar una mirada fresca, aprender de proyectos reales de energía renovable y ver el impacto directo de tus análisis en el negocio. Lo que ofrecemos Sueldo mensual: $34,000.00 MXN brutos mensuales. Esquema de trabajo híbrido (esquema flexible con días de oficina acordados). Horarios flexibles (jornada estándar y salidas tempranas los viernes). Ambiente dinámico de mentoría y crecimiento continuo.

Title: Strategy & Analytics Intern

DiDi provides car owners, drivers, and delivery partners with flexible work and income opportunities. DiDi strives to create better life experiences and greater social value, by building a safe, inclusive and sustainable transportation and local services ecosystem for cities of the future. Title: CRM Automation & Personalization Lead
Description: Objetivo general: Liderar, en conjunto con el equipo de Growth/Lifecycles Retail, la transformación de la operación de campañas de Retail: migrar la mayor parte de la parrilla (nacional, regional, cerveza y OXXO Cel) de construcciones manuales a campañas automatizadas y personalizadas, ejecutadas a través del motor de decisioning (PromoWise) y, progresivamente, con capacidades agénticas. Además, coordina la operación y la salida gradual de la agencia temporal de Braze. Es la palanca que permite que el equipo de Retail opere más volumen y diversidad de contenido personalizado, sin crecer en proporción y que reduzca su dependencia de agencias. Responsabilidades del puesto: Liderar la migración de la parrilla a campañas automatizadas , priorizando junto con su líder y Growth/Lifecycles Retail por volumen, impacto y complejidad, para reducir los builds manuales y el costo operativo de Retail. Ser dueño de la ejecución de las campañas a través del motor de decisioning (PromoWise) , operando en conjunto con Growth/Lifecycles Retail y Data las reglas, los pools de contenido, los criterios de elegibilidad y la frecuencia, para que cada usuario reciba la propuesta de producto, y promoción por el canal correcto. Activar en campañas los modelos de propensión, churn y preferencia que desarrollan Growth/Lifecycles Retail y Data , convirtiéndolos en audiencias y disparadores vivos junto con el Squad Tecnología, para escalar la personalización con base en comportamiento real. Coordinar la operación de la agencia temporal de Braze (junto con su líder) , asignando prioridades, revisando entregables y dando seguimiento a SLAs y calidad, para asegurar la continuidad de los envíos durante la transición y su salida gradual conforme avanza la automatización. Ser dueño del control de calidad (QA) de builds complejos y automatizados , estableciendo checklists, pruebas y validaciones previas al envío, para minimizar errores y proteger la experiencia del usuario y la reputación del canal. Diseñar y ejecutar experimentos de personalización , definiendo en conjunto con Growth/Lifecycles Retail las hipótesis y los criterios de éxito y comparando campañas automatizadas contra broadcast con grupos de control, para demostrar el uplift incremental y sustentar la escala. Impulsar casos de uso de campañas agénticas en Retail , definiendo con Martech & Gobernanza los guardrails, niveles de revisión humana y bitácora, para incorporar IA aplicada de forma controlada. Medir y reportar el avance de la transformación , dando seguimiento al % de parrilla automatizada, el uplift, el uso de recursos de agencia y el ahorro operativo, para sustentar decisiones ante líderes y stakeholders relevantes. Habilitar al equipo de Retail , documentando y capacitando sobre la operación de flujos automatizados y del motor, para que el conocimiento no dependa de una sola persona. Colaborar con Martech y el Squad Tecnología , definiendo requerimientos de feeds de producto y promociones, plantillas dinámicas e integraciones, para que la automatización sea escalable y sostenible. Asegurar el cumplimiento de la política de contactabilidad en flujos automatizados , integrando capping, prioridades y exclusiones (REUS, REPEP, ARCO) en el diseño del motor, para que la automatización no se traduzca en saturación. Experiencia directa con motores de decisión en tiempo real (PromoWise, SAS, Pega o similares) y plataformas de personalización. Title: Lider Incentivos y Compensacion Variable

Adicionalmente, garantiza procesos íntegros, oportunos y auditables, fortaleciendo la confianza organizacional en los esquemas de pago variable. Tareas y Responsabilidades Gestión Integral del Proceso de Incentivos: Coordinar, centralizar y validar todos los insumos necesarios para el cálculo de incentivos, asegurando su entrega oportuna y precisa al proveedor externo. Facilitar la interacción con áreas internas clave para asegurar la calidad del proceso y liderar la comunicación oportuna de pagos, políticas, aclaraciones y resultados a Stakeholders. Garantizar la correcta ejecución operativa del proceso, mitigando errores y fortaleciendo la transparencia organizacional. Diseño, Desarrollo y Gobernanza de Programas de Incentivos: Diseñar, actualizar y administrar los planes de incentivos por Unidad de Negocio, asegurando que sean competitivos, justos, estratégicos y auditables. Elaborar y mantener políticas, anexos, lineamientos, capacitaciones y certificaciones que garanticen la comprensión y correcta ejecución de los programas. Liderar auditorías internas y garantizar cumplimiento con procesos, estándares globales y acuerdos vigentes. Title: Product Engineer MX
Description: En Toku estamos construyendo una plataforma de agentes conversacionales para resolver problemas complejos de recaudación de nuestros clientes. Buscamos Product Engineers con mentalidad de founders: personas capaces de entender un problema real, construir un MVP funcional en pocas semanas y validarlo directamente con el cliente antes de escalar la solución. Este rol combina tres dimensiones muy relevantes: ingeniería de software, pensamiento de producto y cercanía con clientes. Queremos trabajar con personas que disfruten construir productos desde cero, que sepan priorizar con criterio cuando existan cambios y no tengan miedo de experimentar para validar una solución en cuestión de semanas. ¿Qué te espera? Reunirse periódicamente con clientes para comprender sus procesos, identificar oportunidades y traducir necesidades de negocio en soluciones tecnológicas. Diseñar, desarrollar e iterar MVPs de agentes conversacionales utilizando tecnologías de IA, validando hipótesis con clientes en ciclos cortos. Construir software mantenible y escalable sobre una plataforma común que permita soportar múltiples soluciones conversacionales. Colaborar estrechamente con Ingeniería, Producto y Product Engineers para definir la mejor estrategia técnica y funcional para cada solución. Tomar decisiones técnicas considerando los trade-offs entre velocidad de ejecución, escalabilidad y mantenibilidad. Participar activamente en revisiones de código, diseño de arquitectura y mejora continua de las prácticas de ingeniería del equipo. ¿Qué buscamos en ti? 4 a 6 años de experiencia como Software Engineer, participando activamente en el diseño, desarrollo y despliegue de productos de software. Experiencia construyendo productos o plataformas B2B/B2C de alta escala, utilizadas por un alto volumen de usuarios o transacciones. Experiencia participando activamente en la definición de funcionalidades y/o trabajando estrechamente con equipos de Producto en contextos ágiles. Experiencia comprobable diseñando soluciones escalables y tomando decisiones técnicas considerando trade-offs entre velocidad, mantenibilidad y escalabilidad. Excelentes habilidades de comunicación para interactuar tanto con perfiles técnicos, como con clientes. Capacidad para desenvolverse en contextos ambiguos, priorizar con autonomía y transformar problemas abiertos en soluciones concretas. Motivación por construir productos impulsados por IA. Disponibilidad para trabajar un 50% del tiempo de forma presencial en nuestras oficinas en Polanco, Ciudad de México Deseable: Experiencia desarrollando productos basados en LLMs, agentes conversacionales, o sistemas de IA. Haber participado en la construcción de productos desde etapas tempranas (0 → 1). Experiencia realizando discoveries con clientes o participando en conversaciones de producto. Experiencia en startups de alto crecimiento o empresas tecnológicas con productos de gran escala. Experiencia en sistemas distribuidos, APIs, arquitecturas cloud o plataformas de alta disponibilidad. Experiencia trabajando con metodologías ágiles y/o trabajando con equipos multidisciplinarios. Disfrutamos trabajar con personas curiosas, que aprenden rápido, toman la iniciativa y disfrutan construir soluciones que generen impacto rápidamente. Si te identificas con esa forma de trabajar, ¡te estamos esperando!

Title: Analytics Engineering Manager, Data Platform & Governance
Description: About LawnStarter LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform. About Analytics At LawnStarter We're a small, senior analytics team supporting the entire company, product, marketing, operations, and finance all run on the data we serve. The foundation is solid: a centralized Redshift data warehouse where all source data lands, modeled in dbt and orchestrated by Airflow, with Segment feeding event data in. You won't be stitching scattered sources together, the platform exists; your job is to make it trustworthy and keep it that way. We're mid-migration to Lightdash as our single BI platform, replacing Tableau and Metabase. Here's the honest gap: everyone on the team today is an analyst. Data quality, tracking standards, and platform hygiene get done as side work, squeezed between analyses. Nobody wakes up thinking about them, which is exactly the job we're hiring for. The Role You'll be the first person at LawnStarter dedicated to data governance, the owner of whether our data can be trusted, and of the roadmap that makes it more trustworthy every quarter. Trust means the quality and freshness of our source data, pipelines, and reports; the definitions behind our metrics; the standards behind our Segment event tracking; the health of our Lightdash workspace; the data feeding our machine learning models; and the security of the data itself. The roadmap means sitting with product, marketing, ops, and finance to understand what the business needs from data, turning that into priorities for the platform, and sequencing the work, yours and, soon, your team's. This is a hands-on role, every manager at LawnStarter builds, and this one is no exception. You'll start solo, with the Analytics team around you: building automation, writing checks, fixing what's broken, and putting processes in place that scale past you. Once you've landed, we open a Lead Analytics Engineer role reporting to you, you'll help choose them, and the function grows from there as scope demands. What Makes This Role Different You're first. Governance has been everyone's side job, so what exists today is yours to reshape, keep what works, redesign what doesn't, and your standards become the company's standards You own the roadmap, not a backlog. Nobody hands you requirements, you discover what the business needs from data and decide what gets built, in what order, and why Whole-stack ownership. Source data to pipelines to dashboards and ML models, you own trust across the entire chain, not one slice of it A live migration to shape. Lightdash is landing now. You get to set up its permissions, structure, and norms before bad habits form, instead of untangling them later What You'll Own The data roadmap - discovering what product, marketing, ops, and finance need from data, prioritizing it against platform health, and sequencing the investment. You'll present it, defend it, and re-plan it as the business moves Data quality and freshness - automated monitoring across source data, pipelines, and reports; catching upstream schema and source changes before they break anything downstream; running incidents to resolution when they happen Data lineage and impact analysis - a living map from production source to warehouse model to dashboard, and the process that uses it: when a production change is proposed, its downstream impact on pipelines, metrics, and reports gets assessed before it ships, not discovered after. The end-state is data contracts with engineering, so breaking changes get caught in their workflow, not ours Lightdash - administration, workspace structure, permissions, and the rollout itself. Your job is to give the company self-serve autonomy while keeping the workspace tidy enough that people can find and trust what's there. Enablement is part of the deal, people follow standards they've been taught, and so is keeping queries fast and warehouse costs sane The semantic layer - we just shipped it for our most critical metrics: one governed definition per metric, in code. You'll extend definition and mapping to the rest and guard the layer against uncontrolled growth as it scales Event tracking governance - our governed Segment event catalog: reviewing new events against its standards, keeping it matched to what production actually sends, and evolving the guardrails (naming, property dictionary, drift detection) as tracking grows AI data readiness - AI agents query our warehouse every day through Brain, our internal AI toolkit. You'll govern what data AI tools can access and keep the warehouse AI-legible: documented, consistent, and safe for an agent to query and get the right answer Data security and privacy - access controls, PII handling and retention under US state privacy laws, and periodic reviews of who, and which AI tools, can see what The governance system itself - the documentation, ownership models, and review loops that keep all of the above running without heroics Problems to Solve Turn business needs into a data roadmap Every area of the company wants something from data, and today those asks reach the Analytics team as a stream of interruptions. You'll build the intake and prioritization that turns them into a roadmap , one that balances stakeholder needs against platform health, survives contact with a changing business, and that your stakeholders can see themselves in. The hard part: saying "not yet" to important people, with a reason they respect. Make the Lightdash migration a step-change, not a re-platforming We're replacing Tableau and Metabase with Lightdash. Done poorly, we trade two messy tools for one messy tool. You'll design the structure, spaces, permissions, certification, naming, that lets stakeholders self-serve at the speed the company needs without creating an uncontrolled dashboard-growth nightmare. The hard part: autonomy and tidiness pull in opposite directions, and you have to deliver both. Finish and defend the semantic layer We just shipped our semantic layer for our most critical metrics, one governed definition per metric, so "two dashboards, two numbers" can't happen. The unglamorous truth: a long tail of metrics still needs definition and mapping, and a semantic layer only stays trustworthy if someone curbs its growth. You'll own both, extending coverage and keeping one-metric-one-definition true as the layer scales. Tame event-tracking entropy Segment events power our funnels and product analytics, and they're implemented by many engineers across many teams. The guardrails exist, a governed event catalog with naming standards, a property dictionary, a review lifecycle, and automated drift detection against production. What's missing is a dedicated owner: someone who holds every new event to the standard, keeps the catalog matched to what production actually sends, and evolves the guardrails as tracking grows. Without that, entropy wins, events drift and silently degrade when features change. Get ahead of breakage instead of chasing it Today, when production data changes upstream, we too often find out when a pipeline breaks or a stakeholder flags a wrong number. You won't start from zero, an AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent already runs freshness monitoring, metric anomaly detection, and dbt-based lineage checks, but it doesn't yet run at the scale or coverage we need. You'll take detection from partial to comprehensive, extend lineage beyond dbt (Segment events and Lightdash need stitching in), and wire it into engineering's change review, so a proposed production change comes with a downstream impact assessment instead of a postmortem. The end-state is data contracts: breaking changes caught in engineering's workflow, not ours. What Success Looks Like (Year 1) Zero pipeline incidents from unannounced source-data changes - lineage and automation catch them before they break anything downstream, and production changes ship with an impact assessment instead of a postmortem Zero freshness incidents - stakeholders never open a stale dashboard Every area of the business manages on official, well-maintained metrics and dashboards - product, marketing, ops, and finance self-serve in Lightdash against a fully mapped semantic layer; Tableau and Metabase are retired; arguments about whose number is right don't happen. Not because you built the dashboards - because you built the system that keeps them trustworthy Every Segment event has an owner and a standard - new events ship compliant, and degradation gets caught automatically, not by accident Governance runs as a system - documented processes that would survive you taking a month off Requirements Who You Are Governance is your craft, not your chore. You genuinely enjoy making data systems trustworthy and tidy, you're the person who can't leave a broken naming convention alone. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you see governance as a stepping stone to "real" analytics work AI-native. You use AI tools (Claude Code, Copilot, ChatGPT) daily to build quality checks, write automation, triage anomalies, and document as you go, one person covering ground that used to take a team. You also see the reverse direction: AI agents consume our data daily, and making the warehouse safe and legible for them is part of governance now. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything manually A hands-on manager. You've been accountable for other people's output, allocating their time, owning their priorities, and you never stopped building yourself. You write the SQL, debug the Airflow DAG, and configure the permissions personally. This is unlikely to be a good fit if seniority took you away from the keyboard, or if you've never been responsible for anyone's work but your own Product-minded. You start from what the business is trying to decide, not from what the pipeline does, and you can turn a vague stakeholder ask into a prioritized plan. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you need requirements handed to you, or if roadmap conversations feel like a distraction from the real work Automation-first. Your instinct for any recurring check is to build a monitor, not a checklist. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your quality practice depends on manual review and discipline An enforcer people actually like. You'll hold engineers and analysts you don't manage to standards, which takes clear rules, good tooling that makes compliance easy, and the spine to say no gracefully. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you avoid friction or, at the other extreme, enjoy being the department of no This Role Is NOT A big-team leadership role. You start solo and then hire a Lead Analytics Engineer who reports to you; the team grows only as scope demands. If you want to direct a large org rather than build alongside a small one, this isn't it A policy or committee job. There are no governance councils to chair and no binders to produce. When something's broken, you fix it, with code, config, or a conversation A BI analyst role. You won't spend your days building dashboards for stakeholders. You build the platform and guardrails that let everyone else do that well A finished system to babysit. Much of this doesn't exist yet. If you want to operate a mature data platform rather than build one, you'll be frustrated here Tech You'll Touch Warehouse & pipelines - Redshift, dbt, Airflow Ingestion - Fivetran, plus custom Airflow pipelines Event tracking - Segment BI - Lightdash (primary), Tableau and Metabase (sunsetting) AI tooling - Claude Code, Codex, Brain (our internal AI toolkit), and any tool that makes you more effective or efficient Observability - an AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent (freshness monitoring, anomaly detection, dbt lineage) you'll scale up, plus the quality and impact tooling you'll add around it You don't need every box checked. You need hands-on depth in the warehouse/pipeline layer and credible experience keeping a BI tool and tracking plan healthy at company scale. Benefits Base salary: $75k-$120k/year Fully remote: This work needs deep focus, building monitors, untangling pipelines, and we trust you to manage your environment. Async collaboration is the norm Flexible PTO: We focus on results. Description: The IT Innovation & Emerging Technologies Lead identifies, evaluates, and validates new technologies that can improve business performance and strengthen enterprise IT capabilities. The role translates technology trends into practical opportunities, business cases, and evidence-based recommendations for the Global CIO and business leaders. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. It provides technical and functional leadership through technology scouting, practical experimentation, and cross-functional coordination. The role supports handover of validated solutions to delivery teams, aligned with enterprise architecture and security requirements. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Technology Scouting and Trend Analysis Monitor emerging technologies, vendor roadmaps, startups, and industry developments across AI, automation, cloud, data and analytics, cybersecurity, and enterprise platforms. Business Opportunities and Technology Assessment Partner with business and IT leaders to identify challenges and prioritize use cases based on value, feasibility, risk, and strategic fit. Assess solutions and suppliers for integration, scalability, security, data requirements, licensing, total cost of ownership, and vendor viability. Develop business cases with expected benefits, investment requirements, assumptions, and success measures. Proofs of Concept and Pilots Propose pilot scope, cost estimates, stakeholder contributions, evaluation criteria, and go or no-go checkpoints for approval. Build or configure initial prototypes where feasible and coordinate testing with technical specialists and suppliers; document results and recommend adoption, further testing, or discontinuation. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Innovation Roadmap and Adoption Maintain an innovation opportunity pipeline and propose roadmap priorities to the Global CIO, aligned with business needs and IT strategy. Coordinate handover of validated solutions to delivery and operational teams, including ownership, support requirements, and benefits tracking. Partnerships and Knowledge Sharing Build relationships with technology providers and innovation ecosystems; evaluate partnership opportunities with Procurement and relevant stakeholders. Share findings through executive briefings, demonstrations, and workshops that help teams identify practical technology applications. Governance and Performance Engage Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, Legal, and data owners throughout evaluation and experimentation; obtain required approvals before production adoption. Report pipeline progress, pilot outcomes, time to decision, adoption, and realized benefits; track pilot costs against approved funding and capture lessons learned. REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE Technical and Business Expertise Broad understanding of enterprise IT, including cloud, integration, data platforms, cybersecurity, AI, and process automation; ability to assess technical trade-offs with specialists. Practical experience evaluating emerging technologies and delivering proofs of concept or pilots with documented business outcomes. Strong technology research, vendor evaluation, business case development, and financial analysis skills. Communication and Delivery Ability to explain technical opportunities and risks to executives and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority. Strong stakeholder management, structured experimentation, prioritization, and project coordination skills; ability to work independently across countries or regions. Experience and Seniority 5+ years of experience in enterprise technology, solution architecture, technology consulting, digital transformation, or related roles. 3+ years conducting technology assessments, proofs of concept, or innovation initiatives, with evidence of opportunity discovery through validated adoption. People management experience is not required. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field. Fluent English required for global collaboration and executive communication.
